alignments.note: `הָיָה` is written in this verse and takes the English copula together with its subject pronoun (rule 17), so the copula is not the construction's here as it is at 27:1.
The construct `בֶּן` of the age formula takes the *old*, the finite `הָיָה` beside it having already taken the copula; the unit is discontinuous from the verb under rule 25.
Numeral; the ASV reverses the Hebrew order of the two numerals here.
The one written *and* stands between the two numerals this waw joins (rule 42).
Counted noun of the first numeral phrase.
Temporal `בְּ` + infinitive construct recast as a finite clause takes the *when* (rule 52).
Infinitive construct rendered *began to reign*, headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
Suffix on the infinitive construct is its subject and takes the English subject pronoun (rule 18).
`שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה` rendered by the single word *sixteen*, so the two morphemes share one unit under rule 30, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme.
Counted noun of the second numeral phrase.
Finite verb; the ASV gaps the subject pronoun in this coordinated clause, so the verb takes only the lexical verb.

review_notes: Unlike 27:1, this verse writes `הָיָה`, so the copula and subject pronoun go to that verb and `בֶּן` keeps only *old*; each verse is aligned on its own evidence.
The single *and* of the numeral phrase is matched to the waw standing between the same two numerals (rule 42).
